hero.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic and rain to Florida roads
hero.body:
A record-breaking number of Americans are hitting the roads this Fourth of July weekend, with travel challenges compounded by heavy rain across South Florida. The AAA estimates that 72.2 million people will travel at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, marking an all-time high for the holiday. Of those travelers, 61.4 million are making the journey by car, also an all-time record. The sheer volume of vehicles has created congestion on major routes, particularly the Florida Turnpike heading south of Orlando, where Friday's wet weather made conditions especially difficult.

Rain significantly impacted driving conditions as the holiday weekend began. Driver Ed Budd described the situation on rain-soaked roads, saying "Really beautiful until it starts raining and then everyone forgets how to drive." Despite the challenging weather, most drivers continued their holiday trips. Jim Macfawn, who has extensive driving experience, took the conditions in stride. "I have a lot of experience driving, so I just roll with the punches," he said. Macfawn also noted his surprise at the scale of this year's travel, commenting on the high gas prices that would accompany such widespread journeys.

Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations for Independence Day travelers, according to AAA. Experiences varied significantly depending on when drivers hit the road. Carlos Borras and his wife completed a round trip between Orlando and Miami on Friday without encountering problems. "I don't think I saw any traffic, no accidents or anything, so it's been great," Borras said. In contrast, driver Fernando Amado reported busy conditions on the same route, particularly affected by the weather. Amado noted that Friday appeared to be the day when most travelers were heading north, suggesting that the heaviest volume had not yet passed through the area.

For those still planning to travel, the AAA offers specific recommendations to avoid peak congestion. Drivers should hit the road after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday to experience the lightest traffic conditions. The heaviest congestion is expected between 10 a.m. on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday. These recommendations highlight the importance of timing when planning holiday travel, as departure time can significantly impact the overall driving experience on crowded roads during one of the busiest travel weekends of the year.

cards.headline: DeSantis signs $117.6 billion Florida budget, vetoes $810 million in line items
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a $117.6 billion state budget this week, marking the fourth consecutive year of declining state spending. The term-limited Governor exercised his veto authority to cut nearly $810 million in line-item appropriations, declaring he was not trying to set a record after vetoing a record-breaking $3.1 billion in 2022.

The new budget invests billions in accelerated road construction projects, increased teacher pay, and major cancer research initiatives. DeSantis set aside $665 million for Everglades restoration. The Governor said he vetoed items he considered either inappropriate or nice to have. Among the significant cuts, DeSantis rejected $91.5 million designated for correctional officer salary increases.

The Legislature had planned to transfer an additional $750 million into the state's rainy-day fund to prepare for a new constitutional requirement. The House passed a proposed constitutional amendment last year that would increase the mandated cap on the budget stabilization fund, and lawmakers included the transfer to ensure the state would meet the future obligation. DeSantis rejected that transfer along with his line-item vetoes.

Government watchdog Florida TaxWatch had urged DeSantis to eliminate 621 projects worth $830 million that the group labeled budget turkeys. The Governor vetoed 184 of those 621 appropriations. DeSantis also said he does not plan to formally lead any political committee to campaign for a proposed constitutional amendment after the Legislature modified his original proposal, though he indicated he might participate if asked to do something specific. The 2026-27 fiscal year budget takes effect immediately.

cards.headline: Martin County Maritime Response Unit deploys two medic boats for Fourth of July weekend
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit is expecting hundreds of boaters on the water this Fourth of July weekend. The team will have two boats with medics on standby in north and south Martin County.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are expected on Florida waterways this Fourth of July weekend, prompting Martin County Maritime Response Unit to deploy two medic boats for safety coverage. Lt. Brett Harry said the team will position boats with medics on standby in both the north and south areas of Martin County to assist boaters in need. "We're just out there to mitigate anybody that needs help, whether it's something as simple as a stubbed toe to anything cardiac related, or potential spinal injuries, or anything like that," Harry said.

Boaters like Brendan and Ashley Shannon, who launched from Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday with their young daughter and puppy, are prioritizing safety on the water. Harry urged boaters to take precautions including keeping their eyes on the water, designating a driver, and packing life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: Juno Beach Town Council to debate fence replacement at JB-7 beach access in budget talks
cards.teaser: Colony Condos residents say beachgoers are cutting through their private property at the JB-7 public beach access point after the town removed a fence in 2023. The council will take up the issue as part of budget discussions on July 15.
cards.body:
Residents at the Colony Condos in Juno Beach say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. Lori Hill, a Colony resident, said the problem peaks in summer when cars park in resident spots and people push back bushes with coolers, fishing rods and lawn chairs. Hill said residents have been calling police to confront trespassers who become rude when told they are on private property.

The dispute came before the Juno Beach Town Council at a recent meeting, where a town official noted the town is not obligated to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern said a lower-cost solution may be worth exploring, suggesting perhaps a combination of split rail and shrubs. Hill said residents are hoping the town will put the fence back up so they can have their landscaping and private parking.

The council agreed to take up the fence question as part of its upcoming budget discussions on July 15. A fix could cost the town thousands of dollars, though not everyone sees a major issue. Beachgoer Michael House said he has never noticed anyone hopping the fence or shrubs and that there is plenty of free parking nearby.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board filed court documents Thursday opposing a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy who was suspended following social media comments about Charlie Kirk. Theobald, who has worked at the school since 2009, made Facebook posts describing Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In its filing, the school board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone made numerous findings unsupported by competent substantial evidence and contended that Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk constituted a serious offense warranting his removal.

According to an investigation report, Theobald acknowledged authoring the comments about Kirk but said he posted them on his mother's private Facebook page within a discussion among personal acquaintances and did not intend for them to be shared publicly. In her order issued last month, Livingstone cited a Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling stating that disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds on personal equipment with no student involvement violates First Amendment rights. The judge recommended Theobald receive back pay and benefits if reinstated. The school board retains final authority over whether Theobald will be reinstated, and no timeline has been announced for the decision.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County deputies make 15 DUI arrests in impaired driving enforcement
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County deputies targeted impaired driving in a recent operation. The enforcement effort resulted in 15 DUI arrests.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County deputies made 15 DUI arrests as part of a targeted enforcement operation aimed at impaired driving. The arrests came as deputies focused on removing impaired drivers from county roads.

The operation took place ahead of the July 4th holiday weekend, a time when law enforcement agencies across Florida typically increase patrols to address impaired driving. Deputies conducted the targeted enforcement throughout St. Lucie County.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach was selected as one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city to earn the honor this year.
cards.body:
The City of Riviera Beach received the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it one of only 10 U.S. communities to receive the honor and the only Florida city selected this year. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver and recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. Riviera Beach is a first-time winner of the prestigious award, which has been presented annually since 1949.

Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, while Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, stating that the award reflects years of work focused on improving civic health and strengthening trust between residents and local government. The city's application highlighted the Riviera Beach Youth Council, the Citizens Leadership Academy with a 98% completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program that provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. City leaders said the designation positions the community for future opportunities and sends a message to the nation that Riviera Beach is a place where collaboration drives results.

Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, saying "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents.

The prestigious award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. Riviera Beach's application highlighted three key programs: the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership; the Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98 percent completion rate; and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, saying the award reflects the heart and determination of the community and represents years of work focused on improving civic health and strengthening trust between residents and local government.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community raises funds for man who lost fiancée in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiancé Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many belongings.
cards.body:
A Hobe Sound man is leaning on his community after losing his fiancée in a deadly home fire. Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from White's fiancé, Mark. "We received a call from Mark stating that Misty had passed away in a fire," Fenn said.

Friends have launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings. Fenn reflected on her friendship with White, describing her as a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, and playing the piano, and was always the first to lend a hand. The loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured. "Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, and lost him tragically," Fenn said. The timing of White's death adds another layer of heartbreak, as her birthday is the Fourth of July. She passed just a few days before her birthday.

cards.headline: Boca Raton Community High School band to represent Florida at National Independence Day Parade
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton Community High School band will march in Washington D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade on July 4 at 10:30 a.m., representing the entire state of Florida. Only bands nominated by state officials get invited to the prestigious event.
cards.body:
The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned a coveted spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade and will represent the entire state of Florida. On July 4 at 10:30 a.m., the students will march a full mile along the National Mall, from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue. Only bands nominated by state officials receive invitations to this prestigious event.

Junior Lola Cabezas acknowledged the magnitude of the moment, noting there are millions, if not billions, of people watching. She explained the physical demands of marching band, saying students must play, breathe, and walk while maintaining consistent sound. Senior Stephin Restivo said the team is focused on nailing every detail, with everyone able to see what the Boca High band is capable of. Band Director Jenn Girdlestone expressed full confidence that students will put their best foot forward and represent the country well. Senior Lily Schaffer called the opportunity amazing, saying it shows how much the program has grown. The parade will be streamed live on YouTube for those watching from home.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation offers tours, classes at historic Fort Pierce estate
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation in Fort Pierce preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain at the historic Crain Estate. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and architecture every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.
cards.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation in Fort Pierce is transforming the city into an artistic destination while preserving the legacy of the historic Crain Estate. The non-profit organization maintains the former home of Jaxson and Mary Crain, who filled the property with one-of-a-kind items collected during nine trips around the world, including a gazebo shipped from India. Jaxson Crain was a tile worker by trade, and his craftsmanship remains visible throughout the facility on floors, walls, and ceilings. The foundation has kept the estate 90 percent unchanged from the Crains' time there, including original features like the smoking and bourbon room. Guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture are offered every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

The property is known for its peacocks, birds the Crains are believed to have introduced to Fort Pierce in the 1970s. From seven peacocks originally brought to the estate, the population has grown to over 100. One beloved bird named Bob, believed to be 60 years old and identifiable by his limp, is hand-fed daily by staff. The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts international artists with simple but elegant accommodations on the property. The art lab offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels, with one-on-one instruction designed for complete beginners who walk out with finished artwork.

hero.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4% this year on Treasure Coast
hero.teaser: A holiday cookout meal for 10 now costs $73.82 according to the American Farm Bureau Federation, with ground beef up 5.5% and strawberries up 12.4% after a Florida frost.
hero.body:
The tradition of Fourth of July cookouts is becoming more expensive for Florida families. According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, hosting a holiday meal for 10 people now costs $73.82, representing a 4% increase from the previous year. The rise reflects broader inflationary pressures affecting grocery prices across multiple food categories.

The survey data shows significant price increases for several cookout staples. Ground beef prices have climbed 5.5% compared to last year, while hamburger buns are up 7.7%. Strawberries have experienced the steepest jump at 12.4%, a consequence of frost damage affecting Florida crops. Ice cream prices have also risen, increasing 5.3% year over year. These increases combine to noticeably impact the overall cost of planning a traditional holiday meal.

Not all grocery items have become more expensive, offering some relief for budget-conscious shoppers. Potato prices have declined this year, making potato chips and potato salad more affordable options for cookout sides. Corn prices have shown more variability, though locally grown corn from the Glades region can provide good value for those willing to seek out regional producers. This variation in pricing suggests that strategic shopping decisions can help offset some of the broader inflation trends.

Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends several practical strategies for families looking to manage cookout expenses. Comparing prices across different grocery stores is essential to finding the best deals on specific items on your shopping list. Woroch also emphasizes the importance of creating a meal plan before shopping, as this approach helps families cut down on food waste, which represents a significant portion of household food spending. By combining store comparisons with careful meal planning, families can keep their Fourth of July celebration costs manageable despite the overall upward pressure on grocery prices.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient denied insurance coverage hours before reconstruction surgery
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, had her Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield coverage denied less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery involving GalaFlex surgical mesh.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy. Less than 24 hours before her scheduled reconstruction surgery, her insurance company Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the procedure. According to the denial letter, the surgery involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex and was deemed "investigational" with insufficient proof that it improves health.

GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh used in breast reconstruction that remains controversial. While popular among plastic surgeons and FDA-approved for some uses in the body, it is not approved for breast reconstruction and is considered an off-label, investigational, and experimental treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that the mesh's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined." However, Clark's surgeon, Dr. Alicia Billington, uses GalaFlex on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says the product causes the least amount of complications compared to other options. Despite Anthem's denial, Clark underwent the reconstruction surgery with GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago after Billington worked to find a mechanism to make it happen. Last year, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction following investigative reporting.

The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, saying "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several programs including The Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy; The Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98 percent completion rate; and The Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, saying the award reinforces the city's positive momentum and brings back community pride. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football team aims for state title after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.teaser: The Saint Andrew's Scots are putting in the work this summer, setting their sights on a state title as they prepare for the 2026 fall football season.
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots are preparing for the 2026 fall football season with their sights set on a state title. After finishing last season with a 10-2 record and a district championship, the team's second-round playoff exit has left them motivated to go further. Head coach Jimmy Robertson noted that most of the seniors are four-year players, with the majority coming from the middle school, giving them deep knowledge of the program and a track record of success. The program is leaning into a more demanding schedule this fall to compete at the next level and attract new people.

For the Scots, success this season is defined by postseason advancement. Senior Jack Whelche said that while an undefeated regular season is a goal, it means nothing if the team continues losing in the second round of the playoffs. Senior Jack Williams emphasized that the challenging schedule is essential to taking the program to the next level and competing against really good teams. Senior Edmyer St. Jean said the summer workouts add up daily as motivation, pushing the players to work harder so they can finish the season positive and break their record.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient and surgeon speak out after insurance denial hours before reconstruction surgery
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, was denied coverage for breast reconstruction surgery by Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield less than 24 hours before the procedure was scheduled, with the insurer saying the surgical mesh called GalaFlex is still considered investigational.
cards.body:
Three months ago, Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma, the most common type of breast cancer. She chose to undergo a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. Clark had the mastectomy completed, but less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex, which the insurer considers "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body but not for breast reconstruction, making it an off-label, investigational treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated its "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Despite the denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh more than a week later. Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex on most of her breast reconstruction patients and has been a vocal critic of insurance denials, sharing patients' stories on social media and calling for policy changes. Anthem responded that it regularly reviews coverage policies based on medical evidence and that GalaFlex "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy" without FDA approval. Last year, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction after investigative reporting.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Drop Pitching Duel to Tampa Tarpons at Clover Park
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie Mets could not break through offensively Friday night, falling 1-0 to the Tampa Tarpons in a sharp pitching matchup at Clover Park. The game drew 3,797 fans and featu
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets could not break through offensively Friday night, falling 1-0 to the Tampa Tarpons in a sharp pitching matchup at Clover Park. The game drew 3,797 fans and featured strong pitching from both clubs, but one second-inning run was enough for Tampa. The loss marked the eighth straight for St. Lucie, while Tampa extended its winning streak to seven games.

Tarpons starter Henry Lalane controlled the game for seven innings, striking out 11 Mets batters while allowing just three hits and no walks. Lalane continued a dominant stretch after striking out 12 batters over seven innings in his previous start against Dunedin, a performance that earned him Florida State League Pitcher of the Week honors.

St. Lucie answered with a strong bullpen-game effort of its own. Starter Christian Rodriguez worked a season-high 3.2 innings and struck out seven. He allowed the game's only run in the second inning after Brando Mayea opened the frame with a double and Engelth Urena followed with a one-out RBI single.

After Rodriguez exited, the Mets' bullpen kept the game within reach. Tyler McLoughlin retired all seven batters he faced across 2.1 perfect innings, striking out five. Kevin Herget, pitching on a MiLB rehab assignment, added two scoreless innings with two strikeouts. Ernesto Mercedes then worked a clean ninth inning, striking out two batters on just eight pitches.

Altogether, four Mets pitchers combined for 16 strikeouts and did not issue a walk.

The Mets had their best chance in the bottom of the ninth, loading the bases with two outs against Jose Ledesma. Tampa brought in Matthew Tippie for the final out, and he ended the threat by getting Branny De Oleo to ground back to the mound.

Trey Snyder led St. Lucie at the plate, going 2-for-4 with a double.

The Mets fell to 2-9 in the second half and 35-42 overall. Tampa improved to 10-3 in the second half and 45-34 overall.

The teams continue their series Saturday at Clover Park with a special 2:50 p.m. start for the 250 Tailgate Party. Fans can get $5 tickets, with $2.50 select beer, hot dogs, fountain soda and popcorn available during the promotion.

hero.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach Offers Sea Turtle Nesting Programs Through September
hero.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season through September. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. The programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn more about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. The center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Conservation groups continue encouraging beachgoers to turn off beachfront lighting at night, properly dispose of trash and avoid disturbing nesting turtles or hatchlings. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

cards.headline: North Palm Beach Country Club Hosts Fourth of July Fireworks and Pool Party
cards.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
cards.body:
The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

hero.headline: Florida waives state park admission fees through Sunday for America's 250th anniversary
hero.teaser: The Florida Department of Environmental Protection is offering free admission to state parks from Friday through Sunday to celebrate the nation's semiquincentennial.
hero.body:
The Florida Department of Environmental Protection announced that all residents and visitors can explore state parks for free from Friday, July 3, 2026, through Sunday, July 5, 2026, to celebrate America's 250th anniversary. The waiver applies to admission fees at Florida State Parks and includes opportunities for hiking, camping, wildlife viewing, swimming, paddling, and horseback riding. The parks also feature historic sites including forts, battlefields, archaeological sites, and other landmarks. DEP Secretary Alexis A. invited all Floridians, their friends, and family to enjoy the outdoors and support the state's public lands during this significant Independence Day.

Three parks are excluded from the free admission offer: Ellie Schiller Homosassa Springs Wildlife State Park, Skyway Fishing Pier State Park, and Weeki Wachee Springs State Park. The waiver applies to day use only, and all other fees including overnight accommodations, special events, concessions, and rentals remain in effect. The Florida State Park system is the only four-time winner of the NRPA's National Gold Medal Award. Over the last fiscal year, Florida State Parks attracted more than 28 million visitors, generating an estimated $3.6 billion in statewide economic impact.

cards.headline: DeSantis signs $117.6 billion Florida budget, vetoes $810 million in line items
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a $117.6 billion state budget this week, marking the fourth consecutive year of declining state spending. The term-limited Governor exercised his veto authority to cut nearly $810 million in line-item appropriations, declaring he was not trying to set a record after vetoing a record-breaking $3.1 billion in 2022.

The new budget invests billions in accelerated road construction projects, increased teacher pay, and major cancer research initiatives. DeSantis set aside $665 million for Everglades restoration. The Governor said he vetoed items he considered either inappropriate or nice to have. Among the significant cuts, DeSantis rejected $91.5 million designated for correctional officer salary increases.

The Legislature had planned to transfer an additional $750 million into the state's rainy-day fund to prepare for a new constitutional requirement. The House passed a proposed constitutional amendment last year that would increase the mandated cap on the budget stabilization fund, and lawmakers included the transfer to ensure the state would meet the future obligation. DeSantis rejected that transfer along with his line-item vetoes.

Government watchdog Florida TaxWatch had urged DeSantis to eliminate 621 projects worth $830 million that the group labeled budget turkeys. The Governor vetoed 184 of those 621 appropriations. DeSantis also said he does not plan to formally lead any political committee to campaign for a proposed constitutional amendment after the Legislature modified his original proposal, though he indicated he might participate if asked to do something specific. The 2026-27 fiscal year budget takes effect immediately.

cards.headline: Southwest Florida communities stage fireworks, parades, and drone shows for 250th Independence Day
cards.teaser: Fourth of July weekend brings celebrations across Southwest Florida as communities mark the nation's semiquincentennial with waterfront festivities.
cards.body:
Southwest Florida communities are marking America's 250th birthday with fireworks displays, parades, drone shows, and waterfront celebrations spanning from Sarasota's bayfront and Nathan Benderson Park to Manatee County, Venice, North Port, and Fort Myers Beach. Bradenton and Palmetto will celebrate together with festivities on both sides of the Manatee River, including activities along the Bradenton Riverwalk, Rossi Park, Old Main Street, and Palmetto's Riverside Park. Palmetto's 15th annual Fourth Fest at Riverside Park will feature 14 food trucks, 20 artisan and community vendors, a "Lil Firecrackers" kids zone, and live music, with fireworks visible from both sides of the river. Sarasota's bayfront will host its America250 fireworks display beginning at 9 p.m., while Siesta Beach will host its 35th annual community fireworks show from 8 to 9:30 p.m., with fireworks launching at dusk. The Siesta Beach display is funded entirely by local residents, businesses, and community supporters.

Downtown Fort Myers will celebrate with a free concert by Deb The Dynamics and a combined fireworks and drone show at the Caloosa Sound Amphitheater from 7 to 9:30 p.m. Fort Myers Beach will begin celebrations with a parade at 10 a.m. starting at Bay Oaks Recreation Center and heading down Estero Boulevard to Times Square, followed by fireworks around 9 p.m. launched from a barge near Times Square. Venice will host a patriotic parade beginning at 9:30 a.m. at West Venice Avenue and Avenue des Parques, with the America250 fireworks show scheduled to start between 9 and 9:15 p.m. at the South Jetty.

cards.headline: Delray Beach opens 1976 Bicentennial Time Capsule as part of official America250 celebration
cards.teaser: Delray Beach will crack open a time capsule from 1976 during its Fourth of July celebration, one of dozens of Florida events recognized as official America250 partner activities.
cards.body:
Delray Beach's Fourth of July Celebration, a family-friendly tradition spanning more than 50 years that draws upward of 20,000 people, is an official America250 partner event marking the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence. On the Main Stage at A1A, the city will open a 1976 Bicentennial Time Capsule, a message from Americans who celebrated the nation's 200th birthday to those marking its 250th. At 6 p.m., a 60-foot flag will rise at Atlantic Avenue and Seabreeze Avenue alongside the National Anthem and a reading of the Declaration of Independence by the Delray Beach Historical Society.

Beach activities begin at 8 a.m. with the 4's on the 4th volleyball tournament and the Star Spangled Sandcastles contest, a sand-sculpting competition presented by local Rotary and Kiwanis clubs with judging at 11 a.m. Guided snorkel and scuba tours from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. will explore the S.S. Inchulva, the British steamship torn apart by a 1903 hurricane 150 yards offshore. Evening entertainment includes tribute act Let's Groove Tonight channeling Earth, Wind and Fire and DJ SoNyce on the Main Stage, with Digital Vibez performing on the East Road Stage from 6:30 to 9 p.m. A Zambelli fireworks display launches at 9 p.m. Roads close from noon to 11 p.m. from East Atlantic at the Intracoastal Bridge east to A1A, and A1A from Thomas Street to Miramar Drive.

cards.headline: Marion County stages four synchronized fireworks displays for America's 250th anniversary
cards.teaser: Marion County will launch fireworks at four locations simultaneously as part of Marion Celebrates 250, with entertainment starting at 5 p.m. and displays at 9 p.m.
cards.body:
Marion County will stage synchronized fireworks displays at four sites on July 4 to commemorate America's 250th anniversary under the Marion Celebrates 250 banner. Each location begins at 5 p.m. with live entertainment, food vendors, and family activities before fireworks launch at 9 p.m. The four sites are Veterans Memorial Park at 2601 E. Fort King St. in Ocala, Wrigley Fields at 405 E. Highway 316 in Citra, Dunnellon High School at 10055 SW 180th Ave. Rd. in Dunnellon, and the Belleview Sportsplex at 6501 SE 107th St. in Belleview.

The city of Ocala is hosting Fourth in the Park at Tuscawilla Park starting at 10 a.m., a free celebration with live music, food trucks, a kids zone, and games. Ocala-based country singer-songwriter Emma Forgette performs from 10 to 11:30 a.m., followed by Nashville recording artist Cliff Dorsey from noon to 2 p.m. The city is also opening its aquatic fun centers, splash pads, and the Discovery Center for free patriotic pool parties. The Patriot Parade kicks off at Southeast 16th Avenue, heads up to Silver Springs Boulevard, and wraps up near Southeast 25th Avenue in the early evening, with veteran groups, local businesses, and community organizations marching.

cards.headline: Legal scholar highlights voting rights fight as central to America's 250-year history
cards.teaser: The celebration of America's 250th anniversary must recognize the long struggle to fulfill the promise of the Declaration of Independence, according to a new book on founding father James Wilson.
cards.body:
Legal scholar Jesse Wegman's new book, "The Lost Founder: James Wilson and the Forgotten Fight for a People's Constitution," examines one of only six people to sign both the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution. Wilson recognized that "the supreme, absolute, and uncontrollable authority remains with the people," as he stated in 1787. The book arrives as the nation approaches its 250th anniversary, reminding readers that America's story is fundamentally a struggle to fulfill the promise of the Declaration of Independence, with voting rights at its center from the beginning.

In 1776, only white men who owned property could vote. Pennsylvania's radical new charter, authored principally by Benjamin Franklin, extended voting rights to all men, including those without property and many Black men. Franklin famously explained that a man owning a jackass worth fifty dollars could vote, but if the animal died before the next election, the man became more experienced yet lost his voting right. John Adams, writing Massachusetts' constitution, warned that expanding suffrage would lead to demands from women, young people, and those without money. Property requirements ended during Andrew Jackson's presidency, Black men gained voting rights partly through military service during the Civil War, women won the 19th Amendment during the Progressive Era, and the Voting Rights Act of 1965 created a multiracial democracy in the United States for the first time.

cards.headline: Florida events tracked on national America250 calendar for semiquincentennial weekend
cards.teaser: Florida communities are listed among dozens of official America250 partner events for the nation's 250th Independence Day celebration.
cards.body:
July 4 marks the semiquincentennial, the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence. The milestone is being commemorated through America250, the nonpartisan initiative of the U.S. Semiquincentennial Commission that Congress created in 2016. Organizers are billing the July 3-5 weekend as the largest synchronized Fourth in U.S. history, with signature events in New York, Philadelphia, and Los Angeles alongside Main Street celebrations in towns across the country.

Delray Beach is among dozens of Florida entries on the national America250 calendar as an official partner event. The city's Fourth of July Celebration, a family-friendly tradition for more than 50 years that draws upward of 20,000 people, will feature a 60-foot flag rising at Atlantic Avenue and Seabreeze Avenue at 6 p.m. alongside the National Anthem and a reading of the Declaration of Independence by the Delray Beach Historical Society. The beach program begins at 8 a.m. with the 4s on the 4th volleyball tournament and the Star Spangled Sandcastles contest. Evening activities include tribute act Let's Groove Tonight and DJ SoNyce on the Main Stage, with a Zambelli fireworks display at 9 p.m. Roads close from noon to 11 p.m., and the city offers free FreeBee rides downtown.

hero.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic and rain to Florida roads
hero.body:
A record-breaking number of Americans are hitting the roads this Fourth of July weekend, with travel challenges compounded by heavy rain across South Florida. The AAA estimates that 72.2 million people will travel at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, marking an all-time high for the holiday. Of those travelers, 61.4 million are making the journey by car, also an all-time record. The sheer volume of vehicles has created congestion on major routes, particularly the Florida Turnpike heading south of Orlando, where Friday's wet weather made conditions especially difficult.

Rain significantly impacted driving conditions as the holiday weekend began. Driver Ed Budd described the situation on rain-soaked roads, saying "Really beautiful until it starts raining and then everyone forgets how to drive." Despite the challenging weather, most drivers continued their holiday trips. Jim Macfawn, who has extensive driving experience, took the conditions in stride. "I have a lot of experience driving, so I just roll with the punches," he said. Macfawn also noted his surprise at the scale of this year's travel, commenting on the high gas prices that would accompany such widespread journeys.

Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations for Independence Day travelers, according to AAA. Experiences varied significantly depending on when drivers hit the road. Carlos Borras and his wife completed a round trip between Orlando and Miami on Friday without encountering problems. "I don't think I saw any traffic, no accidents or anything, so it's been great," Borras said. In contrast, driver Fernando Amado reported busy conditions on the same route, particularly affected by the weather. Amado noted that Friday appeared to be the day when most travelers were heading north, suggesting that the heaviest volume had not yet passed through the area.

For those still planning to travel, the AAA offers specific recommendations to avoid peak congestion. Drivers should hit the road after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday to experience the lightest traffic conditions. The heaviest congestion is expected between 10 a.m. on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday. These recommendations highlight the importance of timing when planning holiday travel, as departure time can significantly impact the overall driving experience on crowded roads during one of the busiest travel weekends of the year.

cards.teaser: A Florida resident discovered a large alligator using their swimming pool.
cards.body:
A Florida homeowner found a seven-foot alligator lounging in their backyard pool. The alligator had made its way into the residential pool area.

The large reptile was discovered by the property owner in the pool. Alligators are native to Florida and occasionally enter residential areas in search of water sources.

hero.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation puts Fort Pierce on artistic map with historic estate and global residency program
hero.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination through its preservation of the historic Crain Estate and artist-in-re.
hero.body:
Rewritten Card Body

The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination through its preservation of the historic Crain Estate and artist-in-residency program. The non-profit organization operates from the former private residence of Jaxson and Mary Crain. Mr. Crain was a tile worker, and his craftsmanship is visible throughout the facility from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items for their Florida estate, including a gazebo shipped from India. The estate remains 90 percent the way it was when the Crains lived there, including the smoking and bourbon room with man paneling, manly bathroom colors, and stained glass leading to a bar on the front patio. Guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture are available every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. The foundation has made a conscious effort to keep the property original and not commercialized.

The Peacock House gets its name from birds the Crains are believed to have introduced to Fort Pierce in the 1970s. From an original seven peacocks, the property now has over 100. Among the flock is a bird named Bob, believed to be 60 years old and recognizable by his limp. Bob has his own bowls and is hand-fed daily. The foundation's artist-in-residency program offers simple but elegant accommodations for artists from around the world. The art lab offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels, with art director Krystal Masters leading one-on-one classes for complete beginners. Masters teaches mediums including sculpting and watercolor, with workshops like paint your pet in watercolor and rainbow.
